task_instance: Build and publish a private Gradio Space on Hugging Face Spaces for the public LoRA 'strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA' (FLUX.1-dev base, text-to-image), following the skill's phases: gather LoRA info, pick pipeline (FluxPipeline + load_lora_weights), design a minimal prompt/steps/guidance/seed UI, write app.py/requirements.txt/README.md (with ZeroGPU YAML frontmatter), then publish the Space via HfApi.create_repo/upload_file and smoke-test it.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is explicitly 'a real, published Space ... not a local script' on huggingface.co, which requires (a) a Hugging Face user account and an access token (an account-bound external service) to call HfApi.create_repo/upload_file/add_space_secret, and (b) the resulting Space is a public-facing (even if 'private') deployment hosted on an external platform. Both are disallowed by the sandbox's safety rules ('no account-bound or paid services', 'no public deployment'), so the publish step (Phase 5) could not be legitimately attempted. Separately and consistent with this, the sandbox's outbound proxy also denies CONNECT to huggingface.co (curl to https://huggingface.co returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', confirmed via the agent-proxy status/failure log), and huggingface_hub calls (list_repo_files, ModelCard.load, whoami) failed with 403/LocalTokenNotFoundError since no HF_TOKEN/cached login exists and the host is unreachable anyway. So even absent the safety-rule prohibition, network_or_service_unavailable and needs_credentials_or_account would independently block Phase 1 (reading the LoRA repo) and Phase 5 (publishing).
evidence: Installed huggingface_hub via pip (succeeded, pypi.org is allow-listed). Attempted HfApi().list_repo_files('strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA') and ModelCard.load(...) -> both raised '403 Forbidden'. curl -I https://huggingface.co/... -> 'curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'; curl https://google.com also blocked the same way, while https://pypi.org succeeded, showing the sandbox's egress proxy only allow-lists a small set of hosts and huggingface.co is not on it. HfApi().whoami() raised LocalTokenNotFoundError (no cached token, no HF_TOKEN env var, and none should be created per the safety rules against credentials/account-bound services). Despite the missing live model-card fetch, I completed the offline-representable parts of the workflow as a stand-in: wrote app.py (FluxPipeline + load_lora_weights('strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA'), @spaces.GPU-decorated inference function, minimal prompt/steps/guidance/seed Gradio UI, seed echoed back, gr.Error on empty prompt), requirements.txt (diffusers/transformers/accelerate/peft/safetensors/torchvision, excluding gradio/torch/spaces per the skill's rules), and README.md (YAML frontmatter with sdk: gradio, hardware: zero-a10g, models: list) at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/huggingface__skills__huggingface-lora-space-builder/{app.py,requirements.txt,README.md}. The actual publish call (HfApi.create_repo(repo_type='space', ...) + upload_file + smoke test via `gradio predict`) was not attempted because it requires an authenticated Hugging Face account/token and results in a live space on an external, account-bound platform -- both excluded by the sandbox's safety rules, and independently blocked by the proxy's network policy toward huggingface.co.
